question: How do substitution-invariant equality statistics of LP2-53’s visually delimited red passage compare with solved GP text and within-page black text?

span.visual_delimitation: Final red ᛏ at the end of one-based text line 6 (the 19th rune), followed by all runes on lines 7, 8 and 9. The span has 1+24+22+4=51 runes. Exclude punctuation, line slashes, the dotted mark after the last rune and artwork.

control_corpus: The output_index column of all eight archived decoded GP reading CSV sections except lp2-56.csv, whose target is a hash rather than prose. Slide every 51-rune window within each section; do not join separate sections. The exact CSV and manifest bytes are hashed below.
same_page_control: All 51-rune windows wholly within LP2-53 page ordinals 0..127, the black prefix before the red start. This is 78 overlapping windows.
measures: IoC=sum_v f_v(f_v−1)/(51*50), adjacent-equal pairs among 50 neighbors, and unique-rune count. All three are invariant under a bijective monoalphabetic rune substitution. Report red values plus distribution min/median/max and empirical positional rank among control windows; overlapping windows are descriptive, not independent trials.
order_control: Exactly 10,000 random.Random(330153) shuffles of the 51 red indices, preserving its symbol multiset and IoC. Report the adjacent-equal count distribution and both inclusive tails; do not promote this post-target shuffle to an authorial cipher model.
interpretation: A match to solved-text statistics is necessary but far from sufficient for a simple substitution. Outlier values are evidence about equality structure only, not proof of another cipher or a translation.
exclusions: Key searches, crib fits, arbitrary red-span boundaries, comparison of literal English letters instead of decoded GP indices, LP2-56 hash target, external corpora and image-to-rune OCR.
